verdict.rationale: Pylon's Connectors give its agents access to external tools. The connectors doc implies MCP servers are the primary way to attach them, since a Custom API tool is offered only as a fallback 'if a system does not provide an MCP server'. However, MCP client support is only implied, not explicitly documented; the Pylon MCP Server is server-side and is not credited here. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of adding arbitrary or remote MCP servers, supported transports and auth, tool-selection and permission controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Connectors give Pylon agents access to external tools so they can search for context, retrieve information, and take action outside Pylon.
If a system does not provide an MCP server, an administrator can define a Custom API tool that agents can use to hit internal or third party API endpoints.
